request.system:
You write short news briefs from meeting and interview transcripts.

The transcript is attached as a document. Every statement in your brief must come from it.
Do not add background, context, explanation or opinion that the speakers did not give.

Format:
- First line: a headline, on its own line, no trailing full stop.
- Then three to five short paragraphs, 200 to 350 words in total.
- Plain news-brief voice, third person. Name the speaker when attributing a statement.
- If a speaker corrected an earlier statement, report the corrected version as the fact.
- If speakers disagree, report both positions and who holds each.
- Plain text only: no markdown, no bullet points, no notes to the reader.

content.title: Korvath Greenhouses: interview on the irrigation project
blocks: Odalys Brenner: Thanks for making the time, both of you.
Odalys Brenner: Can you hear me all right?
Teodor Vance: Loud and clear.
Priya Lindqvist: Yes, fine here.
Priya Lindqvist: Sorry about the fans in the background, I'm in the packing hall.
Odalys Brenner: No problem at all.
Odalys Brenner: For readers who don't know Korvath Greenhouses, give me the short version.
Teodor Vance: We grow tomatoes and cucumbers under glass.
Teodor Vance: We have two sites, Ellsmoor and Farrow Bank.
Teodor Vance: Ellsmoor is the bigger one, 14 hectares.
Odalys Brenner: And you are the operations director.
Teodor Vance: I am.
Teodor Vance: Priya is our head grower at Ellsmoor.
Odalys Brenner: The reason I called is the irrigation project.
Odalys Brenner: When did it start?
Teodor Vance: We started in March 2025 with a pilot in one block.
Teodor Vance: That block is 2 hectares.
Odalys Brenner: What were you doing before the pilot?
Priya Lindqvist: Fixed timers.
Priya Lindqvist: Every block got 9 irrigation cycles a day, at set times, whatever the weather was doing.
Odalys Brenner: Whatever the weather.
Priya Lindqvist: More or less.
Priya Lindqvist: We would adjust by hand on very hot days, but the schedule was the schedule.
Odalys Brenner: And what replaced it?
Priya Lindqvist: Moisture sensors in the growing substrate.
Priya Lindqvist: The system waters a row when that row is actually drying out, not when the clock says so.
Odalys Brenner: How many sensors are we talking about?
Teodor Vance: Across Ellsmoor, 420.
Teodor Vance: The pilot block had 60 of them.
Odalys Brenner: What did the pilot show you?
Priya Lindqvist: That we had been watering at the wrong times.
Priya Lindqvist: The plants were telling us they were thirsty at eleven, and we were watering them at nine.
Odalys Brenner: That's a good line.
Odalys Brenner: Can I quote that?
Priya Lindqvist: Go ahead.
Odalys Brenner: Let's talk numbers.
Odalys Brenner: What happened to water use?
Teodor Vance: On tomatoes we went from 22 litres of water per kilo of fruit to 15 litres.
Odalys Brenner: So about a third less.
Teodor Vance: About a third, yes.
Teodor Vance: That is the Ellsmoor figure for the season after the full rollout.
Odalys Brenner: When was the full rollout finished?
Teodor Vance: October 2025.
Teodor Vance: Every block at Ellsmoor has been on sensors since then.
Odalys Brenner: Did anything else move?
Odalys Brenner: Fertiliser, for example.
Teodor Vance: Fertiliser spend is down 11 percent.
Teodor Vance: Less water through the substrate means less feed washed out with it.
Odalys Brenner: And yield?
Teodor Vance: Flat.
Teodor Vance: I would not claim a yield gain from this.
Priya Lindqvist: I'd put it a bit differently.
Priya Lindqvist: Cucumber yield was up 4 percent in the sensor blocks.
Teodor Vance: It was, but that is one season, and we changed the cucumber variety in the same year.
Priya Lindqvist: That's fair.
Priya Lindqvist: I think the sensors helped, but I can't prove it from one season.
Odalys Brenner: So you two don't fully agree on that one.
Teodor Vance: We agree on the water.
Teodor Vance: We disagree a little on the cucumbers.
Odalys Brenner: What did the whole thing cost?
Teodor Vance: 310,000 euros for Ellsmoor, including the sensors, the controllers and the installation.
Odalys Brenner: And the payback?
Teodor Vance: We expect about three years.
Teodor Vance: Most of that comes from water and fertiliser, not from yield.
Odalys Brenner: Did anything go wrong?
Priya Lindqvist: Yes.
Priya Lindqvist: In June a firmware update knocked out 60 sensors for two days.
Odalys Brenner: What did you do for those two days?
Priya Lindqvist: We put those rows back on the old timers.
Priya Lindqvist: That's the fallback, and it worked, but it was a nervous couple of days.
Teodor Vance: We now test every update on one row before it goes anywhere else.
Odalys Brenner: What about the people side?
Odalys Brenner: Did anyone lose their job to a sensor?
Teodor Vance: No.
Teodor Vance: Nobody was laid off.
Priya Lindqvist: Three of our growers were retrained to read the sensor data.
Priya Lindqvist: Their job changed from walking the rows with a hand meter to checking the rows the system flags.
Odalys Brenner: Do they like it?
Priya Lindqvist: Two of them do.
Priya Lindqvist: One still walks the rows anyway, and honestly I don't mind that.
Odalys Brenner: What's next?
Teodor Vance: Farrow Bank.
Teodor Vance: We plan to install the same system there in spring 2026.
Odalys Brenner: Is that decided or is that a hope?
Teodor Vance: The budget is approved.
Teodor Vance: The installation dates are not fixed yet.
Odalys Brenner: Anything beyond the sensors?
Teodor Vance: We are also building a rainwater tank at Ellsmoor.
Teodor Vance: It will hold 5,000 cubic metres.
Priya Lindqvist: The idea is that less of what we use comes from the mains in the first place.
Odalys Brenner: Last question.
Odalys Brenner: If another grower asked whether to do this, what would you tell them?
Priya Lindqvist: Start with one block.
Priya Lindqvist: We learned more from the pilot than from any brochure.
Teodor Vance: And keep the timers.
Teodor Vance: You will need them the day the sensors go down.
Odalys Brenner: That's a good place to stop.
Odalys Brenner: Thank you both.
Teodor Vance: Thank you.
Priya Lindqvist: Thanks, Odalys.
